title: The love feast
hookLine: a simple shared meal of bread and water with testimonies

cards: In Corinth, the church's shared meal has gone wrong. Some arrive early and eat their own suppers before the others get there. Paul doesn't soften it: "one is hungry, and another is drunken."

A meal meant to make them one family was splitting them into rich and poor. And still the early church kept eating together. Jude's short letter mentions their "feasts of charity," in the King James words.
Charity there is love. Love feasts. Methodists, Moravians, Brethren and others still keep a meal by that name.

teach.b: Acts describes the first believers "breaking bread from house to house," and says they "did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart." Meat there just means food. A table where everybody eats.

John Wesley learned the love feast from the Moravians, brought it into Methodism, and kept it plain on purpose: simple bread or cake, and water, passed from hand to hand, with a shared cup. Nothing to show off.
Corinth's problem would be hard to repeat at a table like that. Then came the real meal: testimony. People stood and told what God had done in their lives that year, that week.

A healing, a rescue, a long night, a turning point. Bread for the body, and a story for everyone else to chew on. Methodists keep it distinct from the Lord's Supper: it isn't communion; it's fellowship.
Other churches keep their own forms.
Moravians hold a lovefeast with sweet buns and coffee, served while the congregation sings.
The Church of the Brethren keeps a love feast with footwashing, a full meal and then communion, following Jesus at the Last Supper.
Different tables, the same old word.

This whole week has been rooms like this: Gelassenheit, a village that forgave, Quaker silence and the queries carried into it, how is it with your soul, a covenant renewed, and now bread and a story.
Anabaptists, Quakers, Methodists: ordinary people carrying the faith together, around a plain table.

how: At a Methodist love feast, plain bread and water are shared and people tell what God has done in their lives; Moravians hold a lovefeast with buns and coffee during singing, and the Church of the Brethren keeps a love feast with footwashing, a meal and communion.

games.q: you're in Corinth, and the shared meal has split into rich and poor eating apart. what does Paul do?
o: let it go; it's only dinner.
rebuke them: one is hungry, another drunken.
cancel the shared meal for good.
games.why: he rebukes them sharply. the early church kept eating together anyway, and the love feast is that table, kept plain.

practice: Remember one table that fed you more than food: a kitchen, a hospital tray, a picnic, a stranger's dinner. Who was there, and what story got told?
If you pray, give thanks for it; if you don't, simply thank the people who were there, wherever they are now.

wordCard.voice: The love feast. A plain shared meal, bread and water, with stories of what God has done, kept by Methodists, Moravians, Brethren and others.

orig.note: Greek: love. in Jude 12 its plural names the love feasts, which the King James calls feasts of charity.

carryVoice: Your line: bread and a story. Plain food, true words, everyone fed. That's the week.
